facts.text: A parameter is an adjustable quantity in a test, its range is the span of permitted values, and a parameterized scenario family is a scenario description with those quantities left open so that thousands of concrete tests can be generated.
facts.quote: A parameter is one adjustable quantity in a test (such as machine speed), its range is the span of values it may take, and a parameterized scenario family is one scenario description with those quantities left open so that thousands of concrete tests can be generated from it.

facts.text: The booklet uses a three-level scenario ladder from automated-driving research: functional scenarios describe events in words, logical scenarios add parameter ranges, and concrete scenarios fix every value.
facts.quote: The booklet follows a three-level ladder from automated-driving research.

facts.text: The logical scenario example for a machine reversing toward a person includes person distance from 0 to 30 meters, machine speed from 0 to 15 kilometers per hour, approach angle and dust density.
facts.quote: A logical scenario adds ranges: person distance 0 to 30 meters, machine speed 0 to 15 kilometers per hour, approach angle, dust density.

facts.text: Chapter 9's example scenario family concerns a machine reversing toward an initially visible or occluded human-shaped object while the operator does not brake.
facts.quote: Chapter 9's example family, "machine reverses toward an initially visible or occluded human-shaped object while the operator does not brake"

facts.text: Chapter 9's reverse-toward-human-shaped-object scenario family varies speed, initial distance, the person's path, slope, load, sensor installation, illumination, visibility, system latency and braking friction; a concrete test selects one vector of these values.
facts.quote: has variables such as speed, initial distance, the person's path, slope, load, sensor installation, illumination, visibility, system latency and braking friction. A concrete test is one chosen vector of these values [Chapter 9].

facts.text: Each parameterized scenario family carries a probability distribution over its parameters derived from field data or expert estimates.
facts.quote: Each family carries a probability distribution over its parameters, taken from field data or expert estimates

facts.text: The probability distribution over a scenario family's parameters enables subsequent rate estimation.
facts.quote: That distribution is what later makes rate estimation possible.

facts.text: Scenario families record constraints and parameter dependencies: dust correlates with dry, windy, high-traffic conditions, and a distribution that ignores this dependency misweights the strata.
facts.quote: And constraints and dependencies are written down: dust correlates with dry, windy, high-traffic conditions, and a distribution that ignores this misweights the strata [Chapter 9].

facts.text: The scenario catalog stores one parameterized family rather than 10,000 copies of a reverse-toward-worker scenario; sampling, search and estimation methods operate on these families.
facts.quote: Instead of storing 10,000 copies of "reverse toward worker", the catalog stores one family, and every sampling, search and estimation method in this part operates on such families.

facts.text: The booklet identifies defensible parameter distributions as the weak point in parameterized scenario-family testing and estimation.
facts.quote: The booklet warns that defensible distributions are the weak point

facts.text: The only off-road scenario library found by the booklet was built for intelligent off-road vehicles, not collision avoidance.
facts.quote: the only off-road scenario library found was built for intelligent off-road vehicles, not collision avoidance [Chapter 9].
